subject: MAP Activation: secure onramp checklist & peering window
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@aureliasystems.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP Activation: secure onramp checklist & peering window

Derek —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our mutual action plan, I'm sending the onboarding checklist we use to scope the POC environment and a proposed cutover cadence. The items we need to close to enable a production-like evaluation are below (we've prioritized the minimum required for the evaluation):

- Org/owner: please confirm the Aurelia org identifier you want us to associate with the POC (example: aurelia-prod-poc).
- API access: we will provision a scoped API key for your team. Confirm whether you want a per-user key or a shared service key for the integration test.
- IP allowlist: share the CIDR ranges your firewall team will use to accept egress from Redwood (we'll provide our egress IPs).
- VPC peering: indicate the preferred peering window (UTC ranges) and your preferred peering method (managed or customer-initiated).
- Security evidence: your security team requested a short SOC2 extract and our temporary data retention policy for the POC — we'll attach those docs.

Proposed timeline (we can compress if you have bandwidth):
- Day 0 (tomorrow): Confirm org id + share CIDR list.
- Day 1: We create API key and post it to the secure vault; we add your egress IPs to allowlist for an hour window for smoke tests.
- Day 2: VPC peering window and end-to-end smoke tests (KV cache and authenticated calls).
- Day 4: Full evaluation dataset runs and perf check.

If that works, I'll loop in Marissa to schedule the peering window and Hannah for operational handoff. I've attached a one-page checklist to make the tasks explicit.

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-map-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@aureliasystems.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP Activation: secure onramp checklist & peering window

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clarity. Answers inline below: 

- Org/owner: use aurelia-poc-2026. That keeps it distinct from our prod org.
- API access: we'd prefer a shared service key for the initial run (we'll lock down access in our CI later).
- IP allowlist: our outbound egress ranges are 34.201.64.0/18 and 52.14.128.0/20 (AWS us-east-1). We've attached our CIDR csv.
- VPC peering: we can do peering as customer-initiated. Preferred window: Tue 2026-05-19 16:00–17:30 UTC (that aligns with our network ops shift).
- Security evidence: sending over our questionnaire and a single SOC2 extract request separately to security@redwood.com.

Two quick clarifications from our infra lead: will Redwood create a route for the peering on its side, or do we need to accept a connection and set routes ourselves? Also: for the shared key, can you issue it with a 30-day TTL and rotate automatically after the POC?

Thanks,

Derek Shaw
Head of Integration
Aurelia Systems
derek.shaw@aureliasystems.com
[Attachment: aurelia-cidr-list.csv (text/csv)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@aureliasystems.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP Activation: secure onramp checklist & peering window

Derek —

Perfect, thanks for the CIDR ranges and the preferred peering window. Quick answers to your infra questions and next steps: 

- Peering mechanics: Redwood will create the peering request and the associated routes on our side; since Aurelia prefers customer-initiated, we'll send a Connection Request ID that your team accepts. After acceptance, we will push the route on our end and confirm.
- Shared key: yes — we can issue a scoped service key with a 30-day TTL and enable automatic rotation at 29 days; we'll publish the key into your vault placeholder and provide a one-time retrieval link.

Next actions (I've assigned owners):
- Marissa Cole (marissa_cole@redwood.com) will create the peering request and schedule the Tue 16:00–17:30 UTC window.
- Hannah Schmitt (hannah_schmitt@redwood.com) will provision the scoped API key (shared, 30-day TTL) and preconfigure the allowlist for the smoke test window.
- Kimberly (me) will send the HubSpot update and the lightweight SOC2 extract to your security contact.

If you can confirm the org id one last time (aurelia-poc-2026) and confirm network ops contact (name + phone) for the peering acceptance, we'll calendar the cutover. Also, I'll include a DocuSign link for the POC addendum if legal needs that in place before we proceed.

Best —

Kimberly Park
Enterprise Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
[DocuSign: https://docusign.com/s/POC-ADDENDUM-DEAL-8742]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@aureliasystems.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP Activation: secure onramp checklist & peering window

Looping back —

I've scheduled the peering window for Tue 19 May 2026 16:00–17:30 UTC and initiated the customer-initiated connection request. Derek, you'll receive the Connection Request ID in a separate email from peering@redwood.com; please accept it from your networkops account during the window.

Hannah: please provision the shared service key and set TTL to 30 days. Add Aurelia egress ranges (34.201.64.0/18, 52.14.128.0/20) to the test allowlist for Tuesday's smoke test and then remove after the verification unless they request longer.

Derek — once the request shows accepted, I'll run a quick health check (auth + sample generation) and post results to the HubSpot deal. Expected smoke test success criteria: authenticated call <250ms median, kv cache hit for repeated prefixes, and no 401/403 from the vault retrieval.

Thanks — will update when the key has been provisioned and when the peering shows accepted.

Marissa Cole
Technical Program Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: peering-request-stub.txt (text/plain)]
